newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: U.S. funds study on Czech Koramo refinery upgrade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. funds study on Czech Koramo refinery upgrade.

text.p: The U.S. government signed an agreement on Monday to fund a feasibility study on modernising the Czech Chemopol Group's refinery unit, Koramo Kolin a.s., U.S. embassy officials said on Monday.

The agreement, through the U.S. Trade and Development Agency (TDA), provides a $200,000 grant to a U.S. firm to conduct the study on how best to overhaul Koramo's dewaxing unit to make it more efficient and environmentally sound.
The U.S. firm making the study will be chosen through a tender conducted in Washington.

Initial estimates put potential costs of the modernisation at over $100 million, U.S. officials said, but they added that the agreement to provide the feasibility study did not mean a guarantee that U.S. firms would get contracts for the project.
Koramo officials said the study should take roughly one year to complete.

Chemapol Group, with holdings ranging from petrochemical companies to arms trading firms and sports teams, acquired its majority stake in the Koramo earlier this month from the state-run National Property Fund.
After the acquisition, Chemapol said it would seek to expand its assortment of motor oils and lubricants which are Koramo's primary products.
